claim: A caller can load a board, score and rank cards per SPEC, apply kill rules, and emit a 7-part handoff packet — with no network I/O and no LLM calls.
api_sketch: Python 3.11+ package `r2s` (or `r2s_runtime`): load_card/load_board from JSON; score(card)->float; rank(board)->list[Card]; killed(card)->bool|reason; handoff(card)->HandoffPacket; optional CLI `r2s rank board.json` and `r2s handoff card.json`. Validate inputs against schemas/ via jsonschema (Draft 2020-12). Public functions are pure given in-memory objects.
non_goals: No GitHub API, git write, or auto-PR
No network I/O in library code
No changing normative SPEC rules (implement only)
No TypeScript port in this PR (may follow)
acceptance: score matches SPEC formula; invalid when H+C+B==0
kill rules: usability≈0, dependency_fit≈0, missing target_repo at design+
rank: descending S, tie-break ascending id, respect max_active_builds
handoff() returns object validating against schemas/handoff.schema.json
examples/board.example.json loads, ranks, and produces a handoff for the top eligible card
No network calls in unit tests
security_notes: Treat all card strings as untrusted; never eval/exec/shell on claim or evidence
Pin runtime deps; prefer stdlib + jsonschema (or pydantic) only
Library must not read env secrets
first_pr_scope: Add src/r2s/ (models, score, rank, handoff, validate), tests/, pyproject.toml. Keep schemas/ as source of truth — do not duplicate rules in prose. Optional thin CLI. No CI marketplace fluff beyond a basic pytest workflow.
